'''Michael Zimmerman''' (born 1953) is an American [[biologist]] and former Vice President for Academic Affairs / Provost at [[The Evergreen State College]] in Olympia, Washington. He previously served in a number of academic and administrative positions including Dean of the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences at [[Butler University]] in Indianapolis, Indiana, and Dean of the College of Letters and Science at the [[University of Wisconsin–Oshkosh]] for 14 years.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Weiss |first=Lori |date=March 22, 2006 |title=Zimmerman to leave UWO for Butler University |url=http://www.advancetitan.com/article_d3da77ff-e571-56e0-8e8b-071bac497b42.html |journal=The Advance-Titan |location=Oshkosh, WI |accessdate=2013-12-08 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131208102041/http://www.advancetitan.com/article_d3da77ff-e571-56e0-8e8b-071bac497b42.html |archive-date=December 8, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Before moving to Wisconsin, Zimmerman spent 12 years at [[Oberlin College]] as a professor of biology and associate dean of the College of Arts and Sciences. Prior to that he worked at the [[College of William & Mary]] as well as [[Hampshire College]].

Zimmerman holds an  A.B. degree in [[Geography]] from the [[University of Chicago]] and a Ph.D. in Evolutionary Biology and Ecology from [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name="mnscience.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.mnscience.org/index.php?id=27 |title=MnCSE - Michael Zimmerman |website=Minnesota Citizens for Science Education |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071008024335/http://www.mnscience.org/index.php?id=27 |archivedate=2007-10-08 |accessdate=2007-10-02}}</ref>

Zimmerman has worked mostly on [[Biological interaction|plant-animal interactions]], in particular when associated with [[pollination]], and has been elected a [[fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="mnscience.org" /> He has an interest in [[scientific literacy|science literacy]] in general, and, more specifically, in the [[creation–evolution controversy]], and organized the [[Clergy Letter Project]] and Evolution Sunday. The latter was dramatically expanded and renamed Evolution Weekend in 2008. He is a regular contributor to ''[[The Huffington Post]]'' and he is represented as a speaker by Ovation Agency, Inc.<ref name="huffingtonpost.com">{{cite news |last=Zimmerman |first=Michael |title=Michael Zimmerman, Ph.D. |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/michael-zimmerman |work=[[The Huffington Post]] |location=New York |publisher=[[AOL]] |accessdate=2010-04-10}}</ref><ref name="ovationagency.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.ovationagency.com/zimmermanM.html |title=Michael Zimmerman |website=Ovation Agency, Inc. |publisher=Michael Zimmerman |location=Olympia, WA |accessdate=2010-04-10}}</ref> In 2007, he was awarded a Friend of Darwin award by the [[National Center for Science Education]].<ref name="ncse.org">{{cite web |url=http://ncse.com/about/friend-of-darwin |title=Friend of Darwin Awards |website=[[National Center for Science Education]] |publisher=National Center for Science Education |location=Berkeley, CA |accessdate=2010-04-10}}</ref>

Michael Zimmerman has written one general book, ''Science, Nonscience, and Nonsense: Approaching Environmental Literacy'', published by [[Johns Hopkins University Press]].<ref name="Zimmerman1995">[[#Zimmerman 1995|Zimmerman 1995]]</ref>
